scope: Source-only bounded audit of requirements 10, 50, 51, 53, 101, 103. No application source or shared acceptance evidence edited.

findings.finding: Keyboard scroll-region enhancement is not refreshed when a pre-rendered native details disclosure opens. The closed reference comparison table has no explicit tabindex, while the observer only watches child-list changes and the other refresh trigger is window resize. Opening details changes its open attribute, so a previously hidden overflowing comparison can remain without the application-provided keyboard scroll region.

source.evidence: Reference Comparison is inside details, with table-panel and no explicit tabindex.
Actual-overflow check, childList-only MutationObserver, resize refresh; no native toggle subscription found.

findings.safe_fix: Schedule the existing overflow-label helper after native details toggle events using a capturing listener, scoped to the opened disclosure. Retain the existing requestAnimationFrame coalescing and preserve author-provided tabindex/accessible names. Avoid a broad attributes observer that can self-trigger on helper writes.
tests: Render a closed details with a genuine wide comparison; open using keyboard without resizing or inserting children; assert an accessible, focusable scroll region appears.
In Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at 320px, Tab to the region and ArrowRight; assert scrollLeft advances and document width does not overflow.
Verify existing explicit region names/tabindex stay unchanged and opening a non-overflowing disclosure adds no needless tab stop.
findings.limits: Source-confirmed missing refresh path. Browser reproduction and actual overflow at each route remain unperformed; this is not a certified runtime defect.

findings.finding: The legacy member profile dialog retains max-height:90vh only. Premium mobile rules add dvh to person-modal and member-workspace, but do not add a dynamic viewport cap to member-profile-dialog. Its mobile behavior can therefore lag the available browser viewport during browser chrome changes.

source.evidence: Legacy dialog gets shared surface styling and border, with no viewport sizing override.
Neighboring modal families have vh/dvh and safe-area treatments; legacy profile omitted.
Viewport meta lacks viewport-fit=cover; actual safe-area behavior should be verified before making global claims.

findings.safe_fix: Keep the existing vh declaration and add a later scoped dvh maximum-height to the legacy profile dialog. Subtract safe-area insets if necessary after a focused layout check; avoid changing document-wide viewport-fit as part of this narrow fix.
tests: Open the legacy profile with every disclosure expanded at 320px and short landscape height; resize viewport downward and assert dialog bounds, final editable field and Close remain reachable through its single scroll container.
Verify 100%/200% text and long names in three browser engines, with native modal focus and Escape behavior unchanged.
Treat browser-emulated safe areas and physical Safari chrome/keyboard as separate evidence; physical checks remain pending.
findings.limits: Source inconsistency is confirmed. Actual mobile browser chrome and virtual keyboard obstruction are unverified, and no physical device result is claimed.

additional_bounded_observations: Reusable surfaces currently have shared visual styling, but this review did not establish a complete surface taxonomy or table comparison-versus-record inventory (items 10 and 101).

Member workspace deliberately has a content scroller plus navigation rail; compute footer can independently scroll at small widths (styles.css:4989). Whether these are justified requires workflow-specific reachability checks; do not remove them from a source-only audit.
